findings.passage: “My goal is to make sure the people of Wisconsin have full confidence in the security and integrity of their elections,” said Green. “Voter ID is a common-sense requirement for every election.”
findings.note: Quoted in his office's release on the Assembly vote for Senate Joint Resolution 2 (voter ID constitutional amendment).

findings.passage: “Election integrity is an important issue in my district,” said Green. “With the rise of activist judges in Wisconsin, we must protect voter ID by way of the constitution. I am confident that voters will approve this amendment overwhelmingly this April.”
findings.note: Same release. He ties protecting voter ID in the constitution to concern about courts.
subjects: voter ID in the state constitution

findings.passage: “With these reforms and constitutional amendments, elections in Wisconsin will be transparent and fair and would make Wisconsin one of the strongest states on election integrity,” said Rep. Green.
findings.note: Quoted in his office's release on an Assembly election package. The release lists ID for all indefinitely confined voters, added checks against non-citizen voting, and Assembly Joint Resolutions 76 (citizens-only electors), 77 (no private election funds) and 78 (voter ID in the constitution).
